column3: This article contains misleading content and fabricated content. It presents unsupported allegations, including the claim that nearly 20 million noncitizens voted, as evidence that the midterm elections were rigged. It also repeats the disproven claim that Barack Obama was born in Kenya, despite official records confirming his birth in Hawaii. These claims encourage readers to accept a conspiracy narrative without reliable evidence.
column5: Very low credibility. The article presents major allegations, such as nearly 20 million noncitizens voting, without verifiable supporting evidence. It relies heavily on speculation, unnamed intelligence sources, and personal anecdotes. It also repeats the disproven claim that Obama was born in Kenya, contradicting authenticated Hawaiian birth records. Although some background details may be accurate, they do not substantiate its central claims.

column3: Uses a short-term temperature decline to cast doubt on long-term warming. It also used a genuine Weather Channel regional forecast in a misleading global-climate context, prompting the channel to object.
column5: It uses temperature observations to support a misleading conclusion about global warming. Although it acknowledges that El Niño and La Niña cause short-term temperature changes, it presents the decline as evidence that concerns about long-term warming are unfounded. It also emphasizes one satellite estimate over land rather than the fuller global temperature record. Its suggestion that El Niño entirely explains the record warmth omits evidence that the long-term warming trend persists after accounting for these natural fluctuations. Therefore, the article fits misleading content because it selectively interprets scientific information to support its argument.
